transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-05-04
Time: 14:00 PT (scheduled 60min, ran 54 min)
Duration: 54 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Raj Patel (Redwood SE), Isabel Ramos (Redwood CSM), Oliver Grant (Cypress Head of Platform), Leila Nasser (Cypress SRE), Marcus O'Neill (Procurement), Sofie Berg (CTO)

Auto-summary (auto-generated, may be incomplete):
- Cypress requested contract uplift and EU edge onboarding timeline; discussed capacity tiers, dedicated vs hosted, latency targets and KMS integration.
- Raj agreed to run microbenchmarks in eu-west to validate tail latency and cost with prefix caching.
- Redwood to send updated uplift quote and contract; customer to confirm final EU regions and internal PO timing.

Topics covered:
- Capacity uplift sizing (QPS, concurrency, burst)
- EU edge/private VPC options and onprem considerations
- Security: SOC2, KMS/HSM, audit logs, SSO/SAML
- Cost/latency tradeoffs: dedicated vs hosted, batching, quantization
- Procurement timeline and next steps

Transcript:
[00:00] Maya (Redwood-AE): Okay hi everyone, thanks for joining. we, um, wanted to run through the uplift ask and the EU edge onboarding plan. I think this is a check-in from both sides to make sure timing lines up.
[00:12] Oliver (Cypress): Yeah thanks Maya. We got your note, Marcus and I have been trying to square internal budget cycles so we can commit to the higher tier, and Sofie's on for the strategic ask.
[00:20] Sofie (CTO): hey all, yeah quick context — our product traffic in EU is growing, predicted 3x by Q3, and we need both lower tail latency and data residency so the EU edge pilot is required before a full contract extension.
[00:33] Raj (Redwood-SE): Great. before we dive in, couple clarifying Qs — what's the current p95 you're seeing today and the model mix? that helps us size the Dedicated pool vs hosted bursts.
[00:42] Leila (SRE): Right now p95 is about ~360ms for our generation endpoints; embeddings are heavier during nightly batch windows but those are low-priority. Model mix is mostly 2.7B open LLM variants and a smaller 14B for high-fidelity responses.
[00:56] Maya: ok that helps. And your concurrency / sustained qps?
[00:59] Oliver: We're at roughly 120 qps sustained across EU with spikes to 450 qps for release windows. We're targeting 250 sustained for the uplift.
[01:10] Raj: Cool. On Redwood side, the main levers are: dedicated capacity (reserved GPU pool) for predictable throughput, plus regional routing to EU edge nodes. We can also set up automatic fallback to hosted model variants to handle spikes.
[01:23] Marcus (Procurement): Quick interjection — what's the pricing delta between hosted and dedicated? I need a ballpark for procurement decks.
[01:29] Maya: Sure — I'll send the uplift pricing in the quote, but ballpark wise dedicated is about 2.2x unit cost vs hosted per peak token because of reserved capacity; we give better throughput consistency and SLA. But with batching and prefix caching you can reduce effective per-token cost.
[01:44] Leila: When you say prefix caching, you mean the KV cache? sometimes in notes I see K V cash in other docs so just clarifying.
[01:50] Raj: Yes KV cache — sorry, poor speech on the call — it saves previous tokens in memory to reduce repeated compute. That helps latency and cost for conversational flows.
[02:01] Sofie: And for EU edge, are we talking cloud-region based or a private VPC?
[02:06] Maya: We offer both. For the pilot we recommend a VPC-connected EU deployment (Redwood Private — it's essentially a private control plane with customer-managed networking). It's what reduces egress and keeps data residency. For full on-prem we can discuss as well but that's a bigger ops lift.
[02:20] Oliver: Ops lift is fine as long as we get KMS integration — our security team insists on bring-your-own-key.
[02:25] Isabel (CSM): We have that documented — we support KMS/HSM integrations, and can provide the security whitepaper. I'll drop the SOC2 and encryption docs after the call.
[02:33] Marcus: Great, procurement will need the SOC2 cert and evidence of audit logs. Also any SSO/SAML templates?
[02:38] Isabel: Yes, SSO templates are in the SSO guide, and audit logs are available in the Console with retention options.
[02:44] Raj: On performance — for the EU edge we typically colocate a fraction of the model pool in eu-west1, and use smart routing to keep warm KV cache locality. For the 2.7B models you mentioned, we can get p95 down to ~120-160ms in many cases depending on prompt lengths and batch. The 14B model is obviously higher but we can use a smaller dedicated set or quantized variants.
[03:06] Leila: When you say quantized variants, do you mean 8-bit or 4-bit? we've seen quality regressions with aggressive quantization.
[03:12] Raj: Yeah good call. We recommend mixed strategy: 8-bit quant for most production prompts, and 4-bit only for non-critical bulk tasks. We'll run evals on your prompt set to measure any quality delta.
[03:23] Sofie: Will the evals be tied to regressions alerts? We want to avoid silent quality drops during rollouts.
[03:27] Raj: Absolutely — Redwood Optimize can tie regressions to prompt sets and trigger alerts. We can set a guardrail threshold for model rollouts.
[03:34] Marcus: On contracting — we want a 12 month commitment with a mid-year uplift clause. Is that standard?
[03:39] Maya: Yes, we can do a 12 month with an uplift addendum. We'll reflect the uplift and region add-ons in the SOW. I will push a contract draft with redlined uplift pricing.
[03:48] Marcus: Procurement will also want lead time for invoicing and PO.
[03:52] Maya: noted. we'll add the billing cadence and PO instructions to the contract doc.
[03:56] [04:00] Oliver: One technical item — during spikes we saw queueing leading to 2s tail latency, which is unacceptable. Does Redwood have autoscale burst or pre-warm strategies?
[04:08] Raj: Yes: we offer burst capacity on top of Dedicated reservations, and continuous batching to keep GPU utilization high without increasing tail latency. We can also provision headroom for your known release windows.
[04:20] Leila: ok will need more specifics — like how quickly can burst scale, and what's the failover if eu region saturates? we want fallback to another region but keep resident data in EU.
[04:32] Raj: Typical burst scale is on the order of minutes depending on capacity availability; we can define a fallback policy to route to another EU region or to hosted fallbacks with data handling controls. For strict residency we can set policy to only route within EU and then use cold fallback policies that mask or redact sensitive tokens.
[04:48] Sofie: That masking solution — is that supported out of the box or custom?
[04:52] Raj: It's part of our routing & data governance feature set — you can configure what gets sent to fallback models. We'll share the routing policy template.
[04:58] [05:10] Isabel: I'm adding notes — action items are: quote, benchmarking, security docs, schedule pilot kickoff.
[05:16] Marcus: On competitors — one of our teams also evaluated Anthropic's managed offering and Vertex's endpoint tiling. Anything we should be aware of to differentiate?
[05:26] Maya: I'd say two things: first, Redwood's strength is unified runtime for hosted/dedicated/private with observability at token-level; second, our Optimize toolkit gives cost/perf suggestions that are actionable — we can show a side-by-side latency/cost spreadsheet if helpful.
[05:39] Oliver: spreadsheet would be helpful. procurement also needs a TCO comparison.
[05:44] Maya: I'll attach a short TCO example and the pricing spreadsheet with the quote.
[05:48] [06:00] Raj: For the microbenchmarks I'll run a small harness simulating your prompt distribution in eu-west1 and capture p50/p95/p99 and cost per 1M tokens for both hosted and dedicated config.
[06:12] Leila: thanks — also can you include cold start numbers? we want to see impact for infrequent heavy endpoints.
[06:18] Raj: yep will include cold/warm metrics and KV cache hit rates.
[06:22] Sofie: timeline-wise we need the uplift in place by mid-June ideally. is that realistic?
[06:28] Maya: If we get signed PO by May 20, provision for EU edge pilot can begin early June and ramp through mid-June. So May 20 is the procurement critical path.
[06:37] Marcus: Procurement target for PO is May 18 but if needed we'll stretch to May 20.
[06:41] Maya: okay good, we'll plan around that.
[06:44] [07:00] Oliver: any blockers from Redwood that would push provisioning?
[07:05] Raj: Usually we need the region list and KMS contacts, plus network allowlist for the VPC peer. Once those are in, provisioning takes 7-10 business days for the EU pilot environment.
[07:17] Leila: we'll get those to you — I need to check our internal security calendar but should be doable.
[07:22] Isabel: I'll send the security packet now (link to security docs: https://redwood.ai/security/packet — NOTE: transcription may mistranscribe links).
[07:33] [08:00] Maya: Anything on SLAs? they asked about uptime and latency SLOs in the RFP.
[08:06] Raj: We offer SLA-backed uptime for Dedicated customers; latency SLOs are part of the Dedicated plan with monitored p95 SLAs for inference endpoints. We'll include the specific numbers in the SOW.
[08:17] Marcus: Are credits offered if SLA is missed?
[08:20] Maya: Yes standard SLA credits — we'll add that language.
[08:23] [08:30] Sofie: Security red flags — we need to know data retention, whether logs are stored outside EU, and access controls for support engineers.
[08:38] Isabel: Logs retention is configurable per account. For EU deployments logs are stored in-region unless your policy asks to ship to a central tenant. Support access is governed by RBAC and an on-demand access request flow; we can set time-limited access and provide audit entries.
[08:52] Leila: Perfect. Also ask — do you have a list of approved HSM/KMS providers? we use AWS KMS and an on-prem HSM for some keys.
[09:00] Raj: We support AWS KMS, GCP KMS, and can integrate customer HSMs via standard APIs. We'll share the integration guide.
[09:08] [09:30] Oliver: OK let's reconfirm the next steps out loud before we finish.
[09:33] Maya: Sure — I'll recap. Redwood will: 1) send updated uplift quote + contract draft by 2026-05-07, 2) SE (Raj) will run microbenchmarks in eu-west and send results by 2026-05-08, 3) CSM (Isabel) will send security/SOC2/SSO docs immediately after call, 4) schedule pilot kickoff tentatively for 2026-05-13 pending PO.
[09:56] Marcus: Procurement to target PO sign by 2026-05-18/20; we'll confirm exact date by 2026-05-11.
[10:08] Leila: I'll send the KMS contacts and allowlist by 2026-05-10.
[10:12] Sofia (brief interruption): sorry, sofie — question about the pilot scope — will it include the 14B model or only the 2.7B?
[10:20] Raj: For pilot, recommend 2.7B primarily with a small smoke test for 14B in a quantized flavor to validate routing and fallback. We'll avoid full 14B production until after performance evals.
[10:33] Sofie: ok that sounds sensible.
[10:36] [11:00] Maya: Anything else?
[11:03] Oliver: No, that covers it. Thanks everyone.
[11:07] Maya: Great — thanks all. We'll follow up with the attachments and next steps.

End of transcript.
